title: Active Storage: Possible arbitrary file write and read in image analysis
description:
Impact
A Rails application that processes attachments with ImageMagick may allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on the server and, when attachments are stored with the Disk service, to read arbitrary files readable by the application process. Those files typically include secret_key_base and credentials for external systems, which may in turn allow escalation to remote code execution or lateral movement to those systems.

Details
ImageMagick selects a coder from the content of the file it is given, and some coders act on files named inside the image rather than on the image itself. Active Storage constrained none of ImageMagick's coders, and the ImageMagick analyzer runs when a file is attached, so an attacker who can upload a crafted file may be able to invoke one. Attaching the upload is sufficient; no variant, preview, or analyze call is required. One specific attack chain has been reported to us, but we do not assume it is the only one that exists.

title: bitcoinjs-lib: Undetected merkle node duplication in block root computation validates a forged transaction list
description:
Summary
fastMerkleRoot pads an odd level by hashing the last node with itself. It does not report that it did so, and checkTxRoots never looks for repeated transactions. A peer can therefore duplicate transactions to fill the pad and produce a block with a different transaction list but the same merkle root. The block hash and block id do not change, so the header still carries valid proof of work. In the proof of concept a real mainnet block goes from nine transactions to ten, and separately to twelve, with the same id every time, and checkTxRoots accepts all three. Bitcoin Core rejects this case through the mutated flag in ComputeMerkleRoot and the bad-txns-duplicate reason in CheckBlock. This is CVE-2012-2459.

title: Action Pack: Possible Strong Parameters Bypass in Parameters#each_key
description:
Impact
ActionController::Parameters#each_key delegates to the internal ActiveSupport::HashWithIndifferentAccess that holds the request parameters, so when called with a block it returns that hash instead of the Parameters instance. The hash does not respond to permitted?, so Active Model mass assignment (new, assign_attributes, update) accepts it without raising ActiveModel::ForbiddenAttributesError. An application that passes the return value of each_key to mass assignment could allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to set attributes that the application does not permit, such as an authorization flag.

This is an incomplete fix of CVE-2020-8164 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-8727-m6gj-mc37), which made each, each_pair and each_value return the Parameters instance but left each_key delegated.

title: Active Storage: Unsigned Content-Type in GCS direct uploads with cache_control
description:
Impact
When a GCS service is configured with the cache_control option, ActiveStorage::Service::GCSService#url_for_direct_upload signs direct-upload URLs with V4, and the V4 signature covers only the Cache-Control and Host headers. A direct-upload client can therefore send a Content-Type of its choosing, and can omit the declared Content-MD5, without invalidating the URL. GCS stores the supplied content type as object metadata, which takes precedence over the response-content-type that Active Storage sets on download URLs, so an uploaded object could be served as inline HTML under the application's bucket path on storage.googleapis.com. Script in such an object runs on the storage origin rather than the application's, but could register a Service Worker scoped to the bucket path and read or replace a victim's later responses for signed URLs in that bucket.

title: Action View: Possible XSS vulnerability in tag helpers
description:
Impact
The fix for CVE-2026-33168 (https://github.com/rails/rails/security/advisories/GHSA-v55j-83pf-r9cq) skips blank HTML attribute names in Action View tag helpers, but it tests the name before converting it to a string. A Symbol name made only of whitespace, such as :" ", is not blank, because Symbol#blank? is Symbol#empty?, so it reaches the attribute escaping, which emits an attribute with no name and produces malformed HTML. The asset tag helpers, such as image_tag, video_tag and audio_tag, symbolize their options, so a whitespace String name passed to them takes the same path. A carefully crafted attribute value could then be misinterpreted by the browser as a separate attribute name, possibly leading to XSS. Applications that allow users to specify custom HTML attribute names are affected.

Releases
The fixed releases are available at the normal locations.

title: File Browser: Trailing-slash directory deletion leaves public shares active for recreated paths
description:
Summary

File Browser v2.63.15 can leave a public directory share behind when the shared directory is deleted through a path with a trailing slash. The share cleanup path calls DeleteWithPathPrefix(file.Path, userID), but the Bolt backend performs the database prefix query with the unnormalized argument before trimming the slash for boundary checks. If a directory with the same path is later recreated, the stale public share becomes active again and exposes the new directory contents through the old public URL.

title: OctoPrint: Stored XSS via saved connection parameters
description:
Impact

title: Rucio: Unauthenticated administrator impersonation through SSH challenge tokens
description:
Summary

SSH challenge tokens are mistakenly accepted as valid credentials during the authentication token validation process.

While an SSH challenge token is intended as a short-lived nonce for use in a subsequent SSH key exchange, the function to validate authentication tokens does not differentiate between these and actual authentication tokens. Because challenge tokens are generated based on an account name provided via headers without requiring prior authentication, an unauthenticated attacker can request a valid "challenge" token for any account (including administrative ones) and use it to authenticate against other API endpoints.

Proof of Concept

The vulnerability exists because SSH challenge tokens are stored in the same database table as regular authentication tokens and validate_auth_token in lib/rucio/core/authentication.py accepts these "challenge" tokens. title: AutoMapper: Uncontrolled Recursion with Constructor Parameters
description:
Summary
MaxDepth, whether set explicitly or applied by default (64) to self-referential type maps, was not enforced when the recursion goes through constructor parameters. Mapping a deeply nested source to a destination built through its constructor, such as a positional record, recurses without bound and throws a StackOverflowException. That exception can't be caught and terminates the process. This bypasses the mitigation for CVE-2026-32933.

The type depth used by MaxDepth was incremented only after the destination object was created. Constructor parameters, including child objects of the same type, are mapped while the destination is created, so each level recursed before its parent was counted, and the depth check never tripped.

- destination types mapped through constructor parameters, including positional records

title: Active Support: Possible DoS vulnerability in Active Support safe_constantize
description:

When constant lookup raises LoadError, ActiveSupport::Inflector#safe_constantize (and String#safe_constantize) builds a regular expression from the requested constant name without escaping it, so a caller that passes untrusted input lets the attacker choose the source of a pattern that the application compiles. title: msgpack-ruby JRuby decoder makes uncapped header-count allocations; a 5-byte message forces multi-GiB OOM
description:
Summary

The JRuby implementation of msgpack (msgpack gem, java platform — pure Java decoder under ext/java/) sizes containers directly from the element count written in the message header, with no cap at all: no equivalent of the C unpacker's SHRT_MAX clamp (since 1.7.3) and none of the buffered-bytes cap that commit c8d42d8 added for CRuby in 1.8.6. title: Soup Sieve: General sibling combinator inside :has() matches untrusted HTML in quadratic time
description:
Summary

Matching a selector that puts a general-sibling combinator inside :has(), such as div:has(a ~ b), against untrusted HTML runs in O(n²) time in the number of sibling elements. A single small document with a few thousand siblings ties the process up for a minute of CPU, so an application that runs a fixed selector of this shape over HTML it doesn't control can be stalled by one request.

:has is powerful, but much in the same way poor regular expressions can be crafted to cause catastrophic backtracking with greedy capturing, has can be used to create non-ideal scenarios that can cause large portions of the tree to be evaluated for one or many elements if not used thoughtfully.

This behavior is not exclusive to Soup Sieve, but browsers make note of these potential performance issues themselves: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Selectors/:has#performance_considerations.

title: Effect: Cookie attribute injection via domain, path, and name fields in @effect/platform makeCookie()
description:
Impact

The name, domain, and path fields of makeCookie() were validated with a regex that allows ;, the attribute separator in Set-Cookie headers. Because serializeCookie() writes those fields verbatim, a caller who passes untrusted input into any of them can append arbitrary attributes to the header.

For example, a domain of "legit.com; Domain=.parent.tld" serializes to session=token; Domain=legit.com; Domain=.parent.tld. RFC 6265 §5.3 takes the last occurrence, so the injected domain wins and the cookie widens to the parent domain. The same trick sets SameSite=None or Max-Age when the caller has not set those options itself.

The value field is unaffected: it passes through encodeURIComponent, which encodes ;. CR and LF are rejected by the existing regex, so header splitting is not possible.

Fixed in #6763 (v4) and #6765 (v3): the shared regex is split into per-field validators that reject ;, and serializeCookie() now validates before writing the header.

Summary

LegalitySyllableTokenizer.tokenize in the NLTK tokenizer package contains an unguarded O(n^2) processing loop. title: compose-lint: Text in a pull request can issue CI workflow commands through JSON and SARIF output on stdout
description:
Impact

0.31.0 fixed GHSA-6f4g-xm8v-pgv6, where text from a Compose file became GitHub Actions workflow commands in compose-lint's output. --format json and --format sarif output never passed through that fix, so ##[ inside a service name or other value reaches the log intact when the output is printed to stdout rather than written to a file. The runner acts on ##[ in the middle of a line, so the JSON layout does not prevent it.

A pull request can therefore create annotations, fold or hide parts of the job log, or issue other commands the runner accepts, when CI runs compose-lint over it, before anyone reviews it. The pass/fail result is not changed.

Affected setups print JSON or SARIF output to a CI log from the compose-lint package, the pre-commit hook or the Docker image. Writing that output to a file, which SARIF upload requires, is not affected. The GitHub Action turns command processing off around each compose-lint run, so it is not affected.
